name: TRL as a governed object, mapped to eligible Indian schemes
statement: Model Technology Readiness Level as a tracked, auditable property of the venture - not a free-text stage label - and map it to the schemes a venture at that level is actually eligible for.
why_it_is_a_gap: Every platform tracks 'stage' as prose. A TRL that a return can be filed against is the object both NIRF and IIC actually ask for, and it is the input a scheme-eligibility check needs. Phase 1 found only 32 of 354 DPIIT-recognised startups appear in the NIRF Innovation table.
evidence_a: 2 of 40 build TRL natively; 32 of 40 are evidenced-absent. The widest technical gap in the matrix.
evidence_u: None. No user in the corpus asked for TRL.
contested_note: Inpart builds it for TTOs. IncuMan builds it for HEIs but is in private beta with no customers.
falsifier: If two vendors demonstrate a live Indian university running TRL to scheme-mapped eligibility, this closes. Watch IncuMan's beta exit.
our_edge: INERTIA. This is exactly the capability that is tedious, unglamorous and requires scheme-by-scheme eligibility maintenance. Incumbents with investor-facing roadmaps will not build it. Phase 5 also shows the budget filter excludes nobody at Rs 1.2L, so nobody is being undercut on price - we would be the only one offering it at all.
confidence: HIGH on absence, UNPROVEN on demand

name: IPR joined to the venture lifecycle, not bolted beside it
statement: One venture record carries the disclosure, the docket, the milestone and the licence. Filing status changes when the venture changes stage, because they are the same object.
why_it_is_a_gap: Six of the ten vendors that build IPR are technology-transfer platforms that never touch incubation. The four that do join it are mostly Indian newcomers with no named customer. A TTO officer and an incubation manager today hold two systems and reconcile them by hand - the same reconciliation problem Phase 1 documented for startup counts.
evidence_a: 4 of 40 build IPR JOINED to incubation, against 10 that build IPR alone. Only Protrak/IISc has a named Indian university, and it is IP-only.
evidence_u: None directly. The FRAGMENTATION complaint category is the nearest signal, and it is about handoffs between people, not modules.
contested_note: Protrak (IISc, IP-only), Inpart, IncuMan, ESI. None demonstrates a full venture-to-licence lifecycle in production.
falsifier: If IncuMan or ESI ships and names an Indian university running joint incubation + IPR, the joined claim narrows to Protrak's reference advantage alone.
our_edge: REFERENCE + SCOPE. StartupHub already competes for the IIC budget line; Protrak competes for the TTO budget line, which is a separate and slower approval chain (Phase 2: 0 of 25 roles have documented budget authority). Winning the IIC budget first and adding IPR second is a sequencing advantage Protrak does not have.
confidence: HIGH on absence, MODERATE on demand

name: The unincorporated venture as a first-class state
statement: Track the idea, the student team and the pre-entity venture as real records with their own lifecycle, which can later convert into an incorporated entity without losing history.
why_it_is_a_gap: Every one of 40 vendors assumes a registered entity with a DPIIT number. The Indian university funnel is mostly before that point. Phase 1 shows NIT Calicut attributing 38 of 55 ventures to an undefined 'others' bucket, and 843 ideas arising from 42 activities - a pipeline of unidentified pre-entity work that no incumbent can represent.
evidence_a: 0 of 40, with no partial implementations either. Nobody has even attempted the easy version.
evidence_u: None. This is a Phase 1 document finding, not a user finding.
contested_note: UNCONTESTED. Which usually means nobody thinks it is worth building - and also that nobody has proven it wrong.
falsifier: If the Phase 1 'others'-bucket and idea-count findings turn out to be a reporting artefact rather than a real pipeline, this collapses. This is precisely what a Phase 3B interview is designed to test.
our_edge: LACK OF INCUMBENT MOTIVE. Incumbents sell to incubators whose revenue comes from accepted cohorts. Counting people who will never be accepted is unmonetisable for them and central to the university's accreditation return. Different buyer, different metric.
confidence: HIGH on absence, UNPROVEN on demand

name: Faculty and Innovation Ambassadors as first-class entities
statement: Model the faculty inventor, the student innovator and the Innovation Ambassador as entities with their own records, so innovation activity is not forced through a 'startup application' form.
why_it_is_a_gap: Every incubation platform in the set begins intake at 'startup application'. Faculty appear only in tech-transfer platforms. But Phase 1 shows the institution splits innovation funding three ways - innovation, startup, IPR - and runs 15,000 college Innovation Ambassadors and 25,000 school ambassadors who are not startups at all.
evidence_a: 0 incubation platforms hold it (Phase 9 'faculty' flag). NOT MEASURED in the Phase 10 matrix, so the 12 later vendors are unscored on this axis - a known gap.
evidence_u: None. Not asked for by anyone in the corpus.
contested_note: UNCONTESTED and unmeasured. The weakest evidence base of the six and the one most in need of a Phase 3B interview.
falsifier: A single IIC coordinator saying 'we already track that in the annual return' closes it. Do not fund this before that conversation.
our_edge: ADJACENCY TO ACCREDITATION. The buyer already produces this data annually for NIRF and ARIIA. It is not a new reporting burden; it is the report they are already late submitting.
confidence: MODERATE on absence, UNPROVEN on demand

name: Guaranteed migration and adoption - the inertia wedge
statement: A scoped, fixed-price migration off forms, spreadsheets and WhatsApp with the data carried over, plus a named onboarding owner for the first two intake cycles.
why_it_is_a_gap: Every vendor claims migration; none sells the guarantee. Phase 11 showed the displaced incumbent is free - two Accubate reviewers moved from Google Forms - and identified the real blocker: programmes that have the means to automate still do it by hand, because nobody sells change management.
evidence_a: 0 of 40 sell migration as a guaranteed engagement. It is a services offer, and services do not appear on feature pages.
evidence_u: STRONGEST user evidence of the six. Three independent routes: the ICUBE institutional record, a six-year university incubator manager, and FRAGMENTATION being the only complaint category with multi-source support.
contested_note: UNCONTESTED. Note the trap: this is also the thing the few incumbents most likely to copy, because it is service work and not a feature.
falsifier: If the ICUBE record turns out to be an outlier - a sophisticated university that most buyers are unlike - the wedge weakens sharply.
our_edge: SEQUENCING. Migration is the only differentiator that generates its own proof: a migrated institution is the reference institution GAP-13 says nobody has. It converts directly into case studies and into the Protrak-style evidence the market currently lacks.
confidence: HIGH on demand, HIGH on absence

name: Department-level tenancy with departmental P&L
statement: Sub-tenancy per academic department, each with its own budget view and correct ownership of IP between the department, the institute and any SPV.
why_it_is_a_gap: Multi-campus is table stakes. How Indian universities are actually organised - by department, with separate heads and separate money - is not. It also determines who signs, which matters given that Phase 2 found 0 of 25 roles with documented budget authority: the Department Head may be a cheaper approval than the institute.
evidence_a: 0 of 40 demonstrably. Phase 9's 'multisite' flag cannot distinguish campus-level from department-level, so this is asserted rather than counted - a stated limitation.
contested_note: UNCONTESTED but unmeasured. Weakest absence evidence of the six.
falsifier: If multi-campus tenancy in any incumbent is already department-granular, this is already solved and we are describing a checkbox.
our_edge: APPROVAL-PATH OPTIMISATION. Phased differently from the product wedge: this may be worth shipping as tenancy plumbing rather than positioning it as a differentiator.
confidence: MODERATE on absence, UNPROVEN on demand

name: Deployment shape an Indian university can actually buy
statement: Phase 8: Fedena sells a FULL college ERP at Rs 1,00,000 flat with unlimited users - below the recommended Rs 1.2 lakh list. Phase 11 found a second free competitor (Univation, free to universities with Google Ads credit). A flat, unlimited-user, sub-Rs-1.5-lakh shape is the price of admission. Meeting it is not an advantage; failing to meet it is a non-starter.
why_it_is_a_gap: Phase 8 comparables, Phase 11 RATING/price findings, OQ-03 still unmeasured - so this rests on competitor prices, never on a stated willingness to pay.
contested_note: Phase 8 comparables, Phase 11 RATING/price findings, OQ-03 still unmeasured - so this rests on competitor prices, never on a stated willingness to pay.
falsifier: A university procurement rule that requires per-user or per-module pricing would remove the constraint entirely.
our_edge: Phase 8 evidence. Fedena at Rs 1.0L flat unlimited users is the price of admission, not an advantage.
